name: HAKO 2000

specs.notes: Engine, power, torque, weight and wheelbase come from Nissan's Heritage Collection (which lists torque as 176 Nm for KPGC10 and 177 Nm for PGC10, both 18.0 kgf.m). 160 PS is a period JIS gross rating. The 5-speed manual and LSD are per supercarnostalgia (not a Nissan document). No credible source for gear ratios or final drive was found, so they are null. Top speed is null because the sources disagree and none is official: jbskyline.net gives 125 mph (~201 km/h) and supercarnostalgia 133 mph (~214 km/h) for the KPGC10, and supercarnostalgia gives 124 mph for the PGC10. Weight distribution was not found.

garage.blurb: The boxy 1970 four-door-turned-coupe that won everything in Japan: a racing-bred twin-cam six that howls to 7,000, rear-drive, a box with a roll cage and a nitrous bottle. Light and alive.

interior.notes: Full, high-poly: dash, seats, rear seat, roll cage, gear lever (works); right-hand drive. No floor handbrake lever (the C10's is under the dash).

source.author: marc.edouard.lepine17 (display name: Marc Ed)
source.attribution: 1970 Nissan Skyline - High Poly Interior by marc.edouard.lepine17 (display name: Marc Ed) (CC Attribution)

limitations: The model is a tuned car (NOS, coilovers, a cage); the numbers are the stock KPGC10 2000GT-R's (approximation).
Gear ratios aren't published: estimates (a close-ratio five-speed).
The 54/46 weight split is an estimate.
